Update 2026-07-19 (auto-dev session): Fixed a real gap unrelated to the pending camera test — saveCourtPositions only wrote the aggregate heatmap (cc_courtProfile) to localStorage, never to Supabase, even though the court_profile column + saveUserProfile mapping already existed for it. A player's aggregate heatmap silently reset on a new device/browser. Also fixed the load side: loadUserProfile already fetched courtProfile from Supabase but never applied it because it lives in its own React state, not on user — now hydrated on login. npx next build clean, deployed (commit cf78482). Does not touch or resolve the still-open Phase 2 real-camera verification, which still needs Lok on an actual court.

(2) low-end Android test device - sidestepped: Phase 2 now measures its own per-tick processing time at runtime and self-throttles off if the device cannot keep up, instead of needing to know the hardware in advance. (3) per-match cloud cost for Phase 3 - deferred, did not build any paid/cloud infra; on-device auto-detect falls back to manual tap automatically if too slow. Shipped: src/lib/motionDetect.ts, frame-difference motion centroid (Canvas 2D pixel diff, explicitly not TensorFlow.js/MoveNet - too heavy and unproven on low-end hardware, a centroid is enough for a heatmap). Wired into ClipRecorder as an Auto-detect on/off toggle next to Recalibrate, shown once calibration is locked. Self-check src/lib/motionDetect.selfcheck.ts passes, npx next build clean, deployed. Still needs Lok: real camera test on his court (no camera in this environment) to judge if centroid precision is good enough.

� Update 2026-07-16: Lok live-tested Phase 1 on a Pixel 9 - hit 2 issues, both fixed and deployed. (1) Rotate-to-landscape warning never cleared on physical rotation - likely the phone's OS auto-rotate lock, not app code (screenshot showed the browser never left portrait). Told Lok to check the quick-settings toggle; also improved the warning copy to hint at this. (2) Calibration was one-shot blind taps with no visual feedback - now the 4 tapped corners become draggable handles with a Confirm/Restart step before locking in, so a slightly-off tap can be fixed without redoing all 4. Also dropped the elevated-3/4-angle assumption from setup copy since the homography math is angle-agnostic - Lok's real setup is a much lower/oblique angle. Still needs Lok to confirm the fixes on his actual court (session only verified via code review + local build, could not exercise camera+auth flow in the automated browser).

Update 2026-07-22 (auto-dev, 5am session): Notion sync only, no new code this session -- both open To-Do items are gated on Lok testing live on an actual court/match, nothing further to build blind. Confirmed via code read + git log that the 21.07.2026 User Comment ("detection seems a bit random", threshold raised 3->4.2) was already implemented and deployed in a live conversation session on 2026-07-21 (commit acc1514, see DEVLOG), not yet reflected in these Notes -- syncing now. That session also shipped full-screen recording (removed dead score header on non-scoring recording surfaces) and a "log this match" prompt on the standalone /live page. npx next build still clean at HEAD (fdb9507). Still needs Lok: real match test to judge if 4.2 stddev is now tuned well enough, or still too sensitive/insensitive.

Update 2026-07-17 (auto-dev, 1am session): Built the natural follow-up flagged last session — clip playback was completely missing, so the detected hit chips led nowhere. Root cause: ClipRecorder's onUploaded callback discarded the uploaded clip URL (only awarded credits) and the detected shuttle-hit timestamps never left component state — neither made it into the saved match record. Fixed the whole pipe: LiveMatchModal now captures both into its live-match state, handleLogMatch carries clipUrl/shuttleHits onto the logged Match, and they persist through the existing live_stats jsonb side-channel (same pattern as pointLog/liveStats — no schema change). MatchDetailModal now renders the clip as a <video> with tap-to-seek chips for each detected hit. npx next build clean, deployed (commit 1e0f5bb). Still needs Lok: real match test to confirm playback + seeking works with an actual recorded clip (no camera/video in this environment).

text.content:
most device-feasible, no cloud cost, fits the static-export/no-backend constraint). Shipped: src/lib/shuttleDetect.ts — decodes the clip's existing audio track (mic was already being recorded for every clip) via the Web Audio API, detects "thwock" transients as energy spikes above a rolling local mean+stddev threshold with a 300ms refractory period so one hit isn't double-counted. Runs automatically once after recording stops in ClipRecorder (both camera and iOS native-file-input paths) — no toggle needed, it's read-only analysis with zero live performance cost. Detected hit timestamps show as a chip list (mm:ss) on the "Recording complete" screen. Self-check src/lib/shuttleDetect.selfcheck.ts passes (synthetic energy spikes: correct timestamps, refractory collapsing, silence produces zero false hits). npx next build clean, deployed.
Caveat: there's no clip playback/scrubbing screen anywhere in the app yet
